- Overestimate prices in the short term (especially after sentiment spikes) — reduce forecast by 2–5% for the next 3–5 days if sentiment > 0.6.
- Underestimate during strong downward sentiment (sentiment < 0.3) — add 1–3% to forecast if sentiment drops below 0.3.
- Avoid overreacting to recent price spikes — if forecast rises > 3% from prior day and sentiment is high, cap the next forecast at +1%.
- Mean-reversion bias: if forecast is > 10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- Lagged overreaction: if true outcome is 2–3 days behind forecast, adjust forecast downward by 1–2% for the next 2–3 days.
- Sentiment-driven overshoot: if sentiment > 0.7 and forecast > 70.0, reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3 days to avoid overcorrection.
- Horizon-specific: for 30-day forecasts, if sentiment is rising, reduce forecast by 0.5–1% per day for the first 5 days to avoid overconfidence.
